summary: Lita Peipina specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. She earned her MA at the University of Oslo (attested 2008) under supervisor Jens Braarvig, and also studied under Jens-Uwe Hartmann.

Litian Fang (1933–2014) worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. After studying at Peking University under Feng Youlan, Yongtong Tang, and Zhang Dainian (ca. 1956–1961), he served as professor, doctoral supervisor, and founding director at Renmin University of China (ca. 1961–2014).

Liu Liqian (1910–2008) was a Tibetologist. He held posts at West China Union University (ca. 1944–1949), the State Council of the PRC's translation administration department (ca. 1952–1958), and the Ethnic Publishing House.

Lloyd W. Pflueger works in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He earned a doctorate from the University of California, Santa Barbara, and served as Professor of Philosophy and Religion at Truman State University (attested 2015).

Lobsang Dargyay (1935–1994) worked in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Rahor Monastery, Drepung Monastery (ca. 1952–1959), and completed his Dr.phil. at the University of Munich (ca. 1971–1974).

Lobsang Gyatso (1928–1997) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He studied under and taught Tendzin Chökyi Gyatso, taught Guy Newland and Yaroslav Komarovski, and served as Head of the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics (ca. 1973–1997).

Lobsang Jamspal (born 1936) is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. Educated at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and Columbia University under Alex Wayman, he taught at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, University of Delhi, and Columbia University (attested 1985–1990).

Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa (1926–2008) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under numerous teachers, including Dudjom Rinpoche, Trijang Rinpoche, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and taught John W. Pettit.

Lobsang Sangay (born 1968) specializes in Tibetology and related fields. He studied at the University of Delhi (ca. 1991–1995) and Harvard Law School (ca. 1995–2004), later serving as a researcher at Harvard University (ca. 2004–2011).

Lobsang Shastri specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as Head Librarian of the Tibetan Section at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives (attested 2003–2006) and as Senior Librarian at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center (attested 2018).

Lobsang Tendzin (born 1939) works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. Educated at Drepung Monastery, Gyuto Monastery, and under the 14th Dalai Lama, he led several Central Schools for Tibetans and served as Director of the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (1971–2001).

Lobsang Tenpa specializes in Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history/archaeology. He completed a Master of Philosophy at Jawaharlal Nehru University under Sharad K. Soni and taught Peter James Gilks.

Lobsang Yongdan works in Tibetology and history/archaeology. After studying at Kumbum Monastery and earning a PhD at the University of Cambridge under Hildegard Diemberger, he held postdoctoral posts at the Max Planck Institute for the History of Science and the University of Bonn.

Loden Sherab Dagyab (born 1940) specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Drepung Monastery and under the 14th Dalai Lama, Trijang Rinpoche, and Ling Rinpoche, joined the University of Bonn in 1966, and founded Tibethaus Deutschland in 2005.

Loden Sherap Dagyab Rinpoche (born 1940) works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Drepung Monastery under Trijang Rinpoche and Ling Rinpoche, directed Tibet House, New Delhi (1964–1966), joined the University of Bonn in 1966, and founded Tibethaus Deutschland in 2005.
Lodrö Chökyi Sengé studied under Rangjung Rigpe Dorje and Kalu Rinpoche, and also taught Kalu Rinpoche.

Lodrö Sangpo works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Ernst Steinkellner, founded the Nitartha Institute in 1996, and served as a senior teacher at the Vidyadhara Institute (attested 2008).

Lokesh Chandra (born 1927) is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Punjab University and Utrecht University (Ph.D. under Jan Gonda), long directed the International Academy of Indian Culture, and later chaired the ICCR and ICHR.

Lopon Tenzin Namdak (born 1926) specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. Educated at Tingchen, Yungdrung Ling, and Menri monasteries, he served as lopön at Menri and Triten Norbutse, and was a visiting scholar at SOAS (1961) and Munich (1969).

Lore Sander (born 1936) works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She studied under Ernst Waldschmidt (ca. 1960–1965) and held positions at the Museum für Indische Kunst (curator, 1987) and Free University of Berlin (lecturer, 1994).
